what: Calibration of "fail loud" directive (2026-04-27, scoped to memory #348/#349 work): "fail loud" on binding-mismatch / hook-load failures means **add clear stderr error logs that surface to editor hook output panels**, NOT interrupt the agent's main flow. The dispatcher's top-level swallow stays — its purpose ("hooks must never break the agent") is correct. What changes: BEFORE the catch absorbs the error, write a structured stderr line identifying the failure class (ABI mismatch, missing dist/, malformed input). User gets visibility; agent keeps running. Same shape for the MCP server: log clearly, degrade tool-call responses gracefully, but don't crash the server. This rules out implementations like `process.exit(1)` on hook failure or unhandled-throw to the parent process.
why: User clarification 2026-04-27: "failiing loudly here means mroee so adding err logs right? not interruiptign main flow?" — pinning down the implementation contract for the loud-error change so a future session (or me re-reading) doesn't over-correct into hook-breaking-the-agent territory. Scoped to hooks/** since that's where the implementation lives.
